
## Display

<a id="s-avatar"></a>
### Avatar

- Id: `s-avatar`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/avatar`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#avatar`
- Caption: Initials on a slab, or a picture pushed through the LCD.
- Note: The picture avatar is this site's LCD, so it is left out. Put an &lt;img&gt; in the slab instead.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `avatar`: `.avatar`
- Use it for:
  - A person or a team, as two initials on a slab: next to a name, in a list, on a card.
  - A face: put an `<img>` in the slab.
- Not for:
  - A status. That is a [Badge](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/badge).
  - A button on its own. Put it inside a link or a button that says where it goes.

Anatomy:

```text

     AR      OP     DS

  ^^^^^^^^  ^^^^^
  1         2
```

1. **avatar** `.avatar`: An ink slab 8 characters wide and 3 rows tall, with the edge. `role="img"` and an `aria-label` with the full name.
2. **small** `.avatar.sm`: 5 by 2. `.hot` and `.ok` color it.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| initials | `   AR` | Two letters on ink. |
| picture | ` ` | An `<img>` fills the slab, cropped to fit. |
| no script | `   AR` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. An avatar is a picture, not a control. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `role="img"` and an `aria-label`: read as "Ana Ruiz, image". Initials alone are read as letters.
- **name**: Next to the name in text, it says the name twice. Give it `aria-hidden="true"` there instead of a label.
- **paint**: The edge is a shadow. Color never carries meaning here: `.hot` and `.ok` are only a tint.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use two letters: given name and family name. | Put a word in it. It is 8 characters wide, 5 when small. |
| Name every picture avatar. | Leave a face unnamed. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.avatar` | The slab, 8 by 3. |
| class | `.sm .hot .ok` | Small, magenta, lime. |
| attr | `role="img" aria-label` | The name, for a screen reader. |

See also: [Badge](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/badge), [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card)

Limits:
- On this site an avatar can be a picture run through the LCD. That is the site's engine; the kit takes an `<img>`.
- No status dot and no stacked group.

```html
<div class="row">
  <span class="avatar" role="img" aria-label="Ana Ruiz">AR</span>
  <span class="avatar hot sm" role="img" aria-label="Operations team">OP</span>
  <span class="avatar ok sm" role="img" aria-label="Design team">DS</span>
</div>
```

<a id="s-badge"></a>
### Badge

- Id: `s-badge`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/badge`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#badge`
- Caption: Inverse slabs for status, brackets for everything else.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `badge`: `.badge`
- Use it for:
  - A status on a thing, in one word: Operational, Degraded, Down.
  - A tag in brackets for what is not a status: Beta, New, Draft.
- Not for:
  - Something that happened a moment ago. That is a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast).
  - A warning a person has to read. That is an [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert).
  - A filter people tap. A badge does nothing: use a [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup).

Anatomy:

```text
1  OPERATIONAL    DEGRADED
2  DOWN   [BETA]
          ^^^^^^
          3
```

1. **slab** `.badge`: Uppercase on a color, bold, one line. `b-ok` lime, `b-warn` yellow.
2. **loud** `.b-hot`: Magenta with the edge. For the one thing that is broken.
3. **tag** `.b-out`: No slab: the word in brackets. For what is not a status.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| ok | ` UP` | `b-ok`: working, done, paid. |
| warn | ` SLOW` | `b-warn`: working, badly. |
| hot | ` DOWN` | `b-hot`: broken. |
| tag | `[BETA]` | `b-out`: a word in brackets. |
| no script | ` UP` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. A badge is text. |

Accessibility:
- **name**: The word is the status. The color only repeats it: "Down" says down in any color.
- **role**: A `<span>`, no role. It is read in place, after the name it sits next to.
- **paint**: The brackets of `b-out` are CSS content. Uppercase is CSS too, so the text stays as written.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| One word, and the same word for the same state everywhere. | Say "Operational" on one page and "Up" on the next. |
| One badge per thing. | Stack three on a row until none of them means anything. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.badge` | The slab. Ink when it has no color class. |
| class | `.b-ok .b-warn .b-hot` | Lime, yellow, magenta with the edge. |
| class | `.b-out` | The word in brackets, no slab. |

See also: [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert), [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast), [Avatar](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/avatar)

Limits:
- Four looks and no more. No violet badge, no dot.
- Not a control: no hover, no focus.

```html
<div class="row">
  <span class="badge b-ok">Operational</span>
  <span class="badge b-warn">Degraded</span>
  <span class="badge b-hot">Down</span>
  <span class="badge b-out">Beta</span>
</div>
```

<a id="s-card"></a>
### Card and dialog

- Id: `s-card`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/card`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#card`
- Caption: Title on a bar of @, walls of #, and a shadow made of colons. Publishing opens the dialog.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui-open`: opens the dialog next to it
  - `data-aui-close`: closes its dialog or popover
  - `data-aui-toast`: shows a toast
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `card`: `.card .lift .bar-title .body`
  - `dialog`: `dialog`
  - `toast`: `.toast [data-aui-toast]`
- Use it for:
  - Card: one thing and its facts, under a title that says what it is. A project, a person, a plan.
  - Dialog: a decision the page has to stop for. Publish, delete, leave without saving. The safe button first, the action last.
- Not for:
  - Saying that something happened. That is a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast), and it stops nobody.
  - A warning that stays on the page. That is an [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert): the same card with a hazard rim.
  - Filters or options on a phone. That is a [Sheet](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/sheet): it comes up from the bottom.
  - Asking before something that can be undone. Do it, say so, and skip the question.

Anatomy:

```text
1 @@ REPORTING REDESIGN @@@@@@
  ##                        ##::
3 ##  Team     Analytics    ##::
  ##  Owner    Ana Ruiz     ##::
  ##                        ##::
2 ############################::
4   ::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
5 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
  . @@ PUBLISH PROJECT? @@@@@ .
  . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
```

1. **title** `.bar-title`: A magenta slab on the top rim. One line, cut with an ellipsis when it runs long. The tag is yours: `h2`, `h3`, `span`.
2. **frame** `.card`: With `.frame` and a tone. The top rim is always @; the walls and the bottom come from the tone.
3. **body** `.body`: The walls, and four characters of air on each side. A `.row` inside gets a row above it.
4. **shadow** `.lift`: The wrapper. Colons in `--deep`, a row down and two characters right. 50 characters wide at most.
5. **dialog** `dialog`: A native `<dialog>` around the same card, in `tone-heavy`. It opens modal, over a screen of magenta dots, drawn here as dots.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| card | `########` | A card has no states of its own. The buttons in it do. |
| closed | ` ` | The dialog is not drawn. |
| open | `. . . .` | Modal. The page behind is inert, under magenta dots, and does not scroll. |
| no script | `########` | The card is plain HTML. Its button opens nothing. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space` | On the button: opens the dialog. The focus moves to its first button. |
| `Tab`, `Shift Tab` | Moves between the buttons of the dialog. The page behind is out of reach. |
| `Esc` | Closes it. The focus goes back to the button that opened it. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: A native `<dialog>`, opened with `showModal()`: modal, the page behind is inert. The card is an `<article>`; the heading in it is what a screen reader lands on.
- **name**: The kit names the dialog by its `.bar-title` (`aria-labelledby`) and describes it by the first paragraph of its `.body` (`aria-describedby`).
- **focus**: On open, the first button takes the focus, so the safe one goes first. `autofocus` picks another. On close, the focus goes back to the opener.
- **live**: A toast shown while the dialog is open goes inside it, so it sits on top and is read out.
- **paint**: The rims, the walls and the shadow are paint.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Name the action button for what it does: "Publish". | Ask "Are you sure?" and offer Yes and No. |
| Give a card a title that says what it is. | Put a card inside a card. The walls double and the shadow falls on nothing. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.lift` | The wrapper that casts the shadow. |
| class | `.card .frame .tone-*` | The box. `tone-mid` for a card, `tone-heavy` for a dialog, `tone-faint` for [Empty](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/empty). |
| class | `.bar-title .body` | The title on the rim, and the walls with the content. |
| attr | `data-aui-open` | On a button. Opens the `<dialog>` after it, in the same element. `data-aui-open="id"` opens that one. |
| attr | `data-aui-dialog="name"` | Names a dialog without an id, for `data-aui-open="name"`. |
| attr | `data-aui-close` | On a button in the dialog: closes it. With `data-aui-toast` it closes and says so. |
| event | `close` | The dialog's own, however it closes. The kit adds none. |
| call | `button.click()` | Opens it from a script with all the kit adds. `dialog.showModal()` alone skips the tap outside that closes it. |
| css | `--dcols` | The width of the dialog, in characters. 36 when missing. |

See also: [Sheet](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/sheet), [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert), [Empty](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/empty), [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- On this site Publish flips the card to live and the button to Unpublish. That is the site script. The kit opens the dialog every time.

```html
<div>
  <div class="lift">
    <article class="card frame tone-mid">
      <h3 class="bar-title">Reporting redesign</h3>
      <div class="body">
        <dl>
          <dt>Team</dt>
          <dd>Analytics</dd>
          <dt>Owner</dt>
          <dd>Ana Ruiz</dd>
          <dt>Status</dt>
          <dd>draft</dd>
        </dl>
        <div class="row">
          <button class="btn btn-primary frame tone-heavy" type="button" data-aui-open><span class="mid"><span class="label">Publish</span></span></button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </article>
  </div>
  <dialog>
    <div class="lift">
      <div class="card frame tone-heavy">
        <h2 class="bar-title">Publish project?</h2>
        <div class="body">
          <p>Reporting redesign will be visible to anyone with the link. You can unpublish it at any time.</p>
          <div class="row">
            <button class="btn frame tone-light" type="button" data-aui-close><span class="mid"><span class="label">Cancel</span></span></button>
            <button class="btn btn-primary frame tone-heavy" type="button" data-aui-close data-aui-toast="Published Reporting redesign."><span class="mid"><span class="label">Publish</span></span></button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </dialog>
</div>
```

<a id="s-details"></a>
### Details

- Id: `s-details`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/details`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#details`
- Caption: A native details element. The marker flips between [+] and [-] and the answer decodes as it opens.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `details`: `.acc`
- Use it for:
  - Answers people look for one at a time: questions, fine print, the long version.
  - Content that is fine to skip. It stays on the page, where find in page reaches it.
- Not for:
  - Anything most people need. Show it.
  - Views of one thing where exactly one shows. That is [Tabs](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tabs).
  - Navigation. A list of links does that.

Anatomy:

```text
1 [-] What ships in the kit?
3     Twenty-eight components,
      one CSS and one JS.
4 - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
2 [+] Can I change them?
```

1. **question** `summary`: The `<summary>`, after a [+] or [-]. The whole row takes the tap, 45px tall.
2. **details** `.acc`: A native `<details class="acc">`. Closed here. `open` starts it open.
3. **answer** `.acc p`: Indented 4 characters, muted.
4. **rule** `.acc`: A faint rule under each one, paint.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| closed | `[+]` | [+] in magenta. |
| open | `[-]` | [-] in lime, and the answer under it. |
| focus | `[+]` | The marker turns into a slab in the focus color. |
| no script | `[+]` | Opens and closes. It is native. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | To each question. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens it, or closes it. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: Native `<details>` and `<summary>`: read as a button that is collapsed or expanded.
- **paint**: The marker is CSS content with empty alt text. The browser's own triangle is gone.
- **focus**: The focus stays on the question. The answer is next in reading order.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Write the question the way people ask it. | Title it with a noun: "Pricing". |
| Keep answers to two or three lines. | Hide a whole page in one. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.acc` | On the `<details>`. |
| attr | `open` | Starts it open. The browser keeps it in step. |
| attr | `name` | The same `name` on several makes them close each other, in browsers that support it. |
| event | `toggle` | The details' own, on open and close. |

See also: [Tabs](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tabs), [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card)

Limits:
- On this site the answer decodes as it opens and a sound plays. The kit opens it plainly.

```html
<div>
  <details class="acc">
    <summary>What ships in the kit?</summary>
    <p>Thirty-two components in two files, one CSS and one JS. No build step. Link them once, then copy any component.</p>
  </details>
  <details class="acc">
    <summary>Can I change the characters?</summary>
    <p>Yes. Every frame reads its characters from two custom properties, so a new tone is two strings.</p>
  </details>
</div>
```

<a id="s-kbd"></a>
### Kbd

- Id: `s-kbd`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/kbd`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#kbd`
- Caption: Shortcuts, as keys in brackets. These ones work on this page.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `kbd`: `kbd .kbds`
- Use it for:
  - A shortcut, written the way the key looks: [/] search, [g] glitch.
  - A key name inside a sentence: press [Esc] to close.
- Not for:
  - A button. A key hint does nothing when tapped.
  - Code. That is `<code>`.
  - A hint on a menu item that nobody can press. In a [Dropdown](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/dropdown) it becomes part of the item's name.

Anatomy:

```text
1 [/] search      [g] glitch
  [<] [>] move    [space] fire
   ^
   2
```

1. **grid** `.kbds`: A grid of hints, 16 characters a column at least.
2. **key** `kbd`: The key in brackets, bold ink. The brackets are CSS content.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| key | `[/]` | Bold ink in brackets. |
| in a menu | `[d]` | Takes the color of its row, slab included. |
| no script | `[/]` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. A kbd is text. |

Accessibility:
- **name**: Write the key out, `<kbd>space</kbd>`, not a glyph only a sighted person decodes. For &lt; and &gt; a screen reader says "less than" and "greater than".
- **paint**: The brackets are CSS content without an empty alt, so some screen readers read "left bracket" too.
- **state**: Put `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control the shortcut runs. Then a screen reader says it there.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Show shortcuts that work on the page they are on. | List shortcuts that only work somewhere else. |
| Write the key as it is printed on it: Esc, Tab, Ctrl. | Invent names: "the slash key thing". |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `kbd` | The element. Bold ink, in brackets. |
| class | `.kbds` | A grid of hints. |

See also: [Command](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/command), [Tooltip](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tooltip), [Dropdown](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/dropdown)

Limits:
- It shows a key. It does not bind one: the shortcut is your script.
- Its brackets can be read out. The rims of the other components cannot.

```html
<div class="kbds">
  <span><kbd>/</kbd> search</span>
  <span><kbd>g</kbd> glitch</span>
  <span><kbd>&lt;</kbd> <kbd>&gt;</kbd> move</span>
  <span><kbd>space</kbd> fire</span>
</div>
```

<a id="s-picture"></a>
### Picture

- Id: `s-picture`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/picture`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: no, site only
- Caption: An LCD panel cut into twelve sectors. Every cell is three subpixels and each sector can run its own mode. Tap a sector. Site only, not in the kit.
- Note: Site only, not in the kit. The LCD panel is drawn by this site's engine. The mode switches are a Segment, which is in the kit. Reference markup. These classes are site-only: bezel, lcd, pic. Their css is not in ascii-ui.css, so write your own. The rest is in ascii-ui.css already.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `segment`: `.tgroup`
- Site only: Site only, not in the kit. The LCD panel is drawn by this site's engine.
- Use it for:
  - A picture on this site: the four scenes, or your own photo, drawn as cells of three subpixels.
  - Showing what the three modes do to the same image: RGB, Mono, ASCII.
- Not for:
  - A photo people need to see clearly. That is an `<img>`.
  - Anything you paste from the kit. It is not in it: put an `<img>` in an [Avatar](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/avatar) or a card.

Anatomy:

```text
1 ...... :::::: ====== ++++++
  ****** ###### %%%%%% @@@@@@
  ++++++ ====== :::::: ......
  ^^^^^^
  2
3   RGB    MONO    ASCII
4 Buenos Aires, 19:42.
```

1. **panel** `canvas.lcd`: A `<canvas>` with `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that says what is in it. 64 by 48 cells, drawn by the site's engine.
2. **sector** `canvas`: One of twelve, four across and three down. A tap moves it to the next mode, and it glitches for a beat.
3. **mode** `.tgroup`: A [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup): the mode of the whole panel. Picking one puts every sector back to it.
4. **caption** `figcaption`: What the picture is, in words. A photo you load says so here.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| running | `.:=+*#%@` | The scene, moving, in the picked mode. |
| sector tapped | `@%#*+=:.` | That sector goes to the next mode: RGB, Mono, ASCII. |
| focus | `@@@@@@@@` | A rim in the focus color around the sector the arrows are on. |
| your photo | `.:=+*#%@` | Cropped to fit. It never leaves the page. |
| error | `!!!!!!!!` | A file that is not a picture says so in a toast. |
| reduced motion | `.:=+*#%@` | Still. Drawn when something changes, never moving. |
| no script | ` ` | An empty panel. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | To the panel, then the modes, then Load photo. |
| `Left`, `Right`, `Up`, `Down` | Moves between the sectors. It stops at the edge. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | On a sector: what a tap does. On Load photo: opens the file picker. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `role="img"` on the canvas, with an `aria-label` that says what is in the picture.
- **name**: The label stays with the scene, whatever the mode. The caption changes with the picture.
- **focus**: The canvas takes the focus, `tabindex="0"`, and draws the rim of the sector you are on.
- **touch**: A sector is a fourth of the panel wide. Hard to miss.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Say what is in the picture in its `aria-label`, as a sentence. | Label it "LCD canvas". |
| Keep a plain `<img>` for photos that matter. | Push a product shot through the LCD and call it the product. |

Made of: [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button), [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup)

See also: [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup), [Avatar](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/avatar), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- Site only. The kit has no LCD.
- It redraws 8 times a second while it is on screen, and not at all when it is not.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <figure class="pic">
    <div class="bezel">
      <canvas class="lcd" data-scene="ba" data-cols="64" data-rows="48" data-mode="rgb" role="img" aria-label="Buenos Aires at dusk with the Obelisco, rendered as an LCD panel" tabindex="0"></canvas>
    </div>
    <figcaption><b>Buenos Aires, 19:42.</b> Procedural, 64 by 48 cells.</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div>
    <div class="tgroup" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Panel mode">
      <label><input type="radio" name="picMode" value="rgb" checked><span>RGB</span></label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="picMode" value="mono"><span>Mono</span></label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="picMode" value="ascii"><span>ASCII</span></label>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div>
    <div class="tgroup" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Picture">
      <label><input type="radio" name="picScene" value="ba" checked><span>Dusk</span></label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="picScene" value="desk"><span>Desk</span></label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="picScene" value="mate"><span>Mate</span></label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="picScene" value="test"><span>Test</span></label>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <button class="btn frame tone-light" type="button"><span class="mid"><span class="label">Load photo</span></span></button>
    <input type="file" accept="image/*" hidden>
  </div>
</div>
```

<a id="s-separator"></a>
### Separator

- Id: `s-separator`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/separator`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#separator`
- Caption: Splits content without a box. Four weights of nothing, and a rule with a word in it.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `divider`: `.sepd .sepl`
- Use it for:
  - A break between groups inside one box: settings in a card, items in a menu.
  - A choice between two ways, with the word in the rule: or.
- Not for:
  - A box around things. That is a [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card).
  - Space. A row of nothing does that, with no rule at all.
  - A heading. A heading does that.

Anatomy:

```text
1 @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
2 ========================
3 ::::::::::::::::::::::::
4 - - - - - - - - - - - -
5 - - - - - or - - - - - -
```

1. **heavy** `.sepd.heavy`: @ in magenta. The loudest break.
2. **light** `.sepd`: = in ink. The default.
3. **shade** `.sepd.shade`: : in violet.
4. **faint** `.sepd.faint`: - in muted. The quietest, and the one a menu uses.
5. **labelled** `.sepl`: A faint rule on each side of a word.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| heavy | `@@@@@@@@` | `.heavy`. |
| light | `========` | No class. |
| shade | `::::::::` | `.shade`. |
| faint | `- - - -` | `.faint`. |
| no script | `========` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. A rule is not a control. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `role="separator"` on each one, so a screen reader can say where a group ends. A rule that only decorates takes `role="presentation"` instead.
- **paint**: The characters are CSS content with empty alt text. In `.sepl` the word is read, the dashes are not.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Give each weight one job, and keep it all through a page. | Mix four weights on one screen. |
| Put the word in the rule when it is a choice: or. | Put a title in a rule. That is a heading. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.sepd` | The rule, one row tall, with a row above it. |
| class | `.heavy .shade .faint` | The weights. No class is =. |
| class | `.sepl` | The rule with a word in it. |
| attr | `role="separator"` | On each one. |

See also: [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card), [Dropdown](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/dropdown), [Timeline](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/timeline)

Limits:
- Across only. There is no rule that runs down.
- An `<hr>` is not styled. Use `<div class="sepd" role="separator">`.

```html
<div>
  <div class="sepd heavy" role="separator"></div>
  <div class="sepd" role="separator"></div>
  <div class="sepd shade" role="separator"></div>
  <div class="sepd faint" role="separator"></div>
  <div class="sepl" role="separator">or</div>
</div>
```

<a id="s-timeline"></a>
### Timeline

- Id: `s-timeline`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/timeline`
- Group: Display
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#timeline`
- Caption: Events in order. Nodes are @, the wire is colons.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `timeline`: `.timeline`
- Use it for:
  - Things that happened, in order: a project log, a release history, a delivery.
  - Newest first, with the one that is now at the top.
- Not for:
  - Steps a person has yet to take. Number them in a plain list.
  - Things with no order. That is a plain list.
  - News that arrives while you read. Say it in a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast); the timeline is the record.

Anatomy:

```text
1 @@  SHIPPED
  ::  Search v2 went to 100
  ::  percent of accounts.
2 ##  IN REVIEW
  ::  14 comments in Figma.
3 ##  KICKOFF
```

1. **now** `li`: @@ in magenta. Its `<b>` is the title, uppercase; its `<span>` says what happened, muted.
2. **past** `li.past`: `.past`: ## in ink. Done and behind.
3. **last** `li:last-child`: No wire under the last one. The wire is colons, in violet.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| now | `@@` | A plain `<li>`: @@ in magenta. |
| past | `##` | `.past`: ## in ink. |
| no script | `@@` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by, or stops at the links you put in it. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: An `<ol>`: read as "list, 3 items", in order.
- **state**: Now or past is told only by the character. Say it in the words too, or with a `<time>`.
- **paint**: Nodes and wire are CSS content with empty alt text.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep newest on top, and the same order on every page. | Flip the order between two pages. |
| Give each item a date, in a `<time datetime>`. | Leave people to guess when "In review" was. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.timeline` | On the `<ol>`. |
| class | `.past` | On an `<li>` that is behind. |
| attr | `datetime` | On a `<time>` in an item: violet and bold. |

See also: [Separator](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/separator), [Badge](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/badge), [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert)

Limits:
- Two looks, now and past. No failed or skipped item.
- No links or buttons of its own. Put them in an item.

```html
<ol class="timeline">
  <li><b>Shipped</b><span>Search v2 went to 100 percent of accounts.</span></li>
  <li class="past"><b>In review</b><span>14 comments in Figma, 3 of them useful.</span></li>
  <li class="past"><b>Kickoff</b><span>One problem statement, zero solutions. As it should be.</span></li>
</ol>
```

## Feedback

<a id="s-alert"></a>
### Alert

- Id: `s-alert`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/alert`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#alert`
- Caption: A card with a hazard rim. The title says what happened, the body says what to do.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `card`: `.card .lift .bar-title .body`
  - `alert`: `.alert`
- Use it for:
  - Something on this page a person has to know before they carry on: an outage, a limit, a change.
  - Info, `.info` in violet: worth knowing, nothing to do.
- Not for:
  - What happened after a click. That is a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast).
  - A decision. That is the dialog in [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card).
  - An error on one field. That is the message under an [Input](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/input).

Anatomy:

```text
1 // SIGNAL LOST ///////////
  //                      //::
3 //  Probes from 3       //::
  //  regions time out.   //::
2 //////////////////////////::
    ::::::::::::::::::::::::::
4 == HEADS UP ================
```

1. **title** `.bar-title`: What happened, in a few words, on a yellow slab.
2. **rim** `.alert`: `.alert` makes the rim yellow; `tone-danger` draws it in /. `.lift` casts the shadow.
3. **body** `.body`: What to do about it, in a sentence or two.
4. **info** `.alert.info`: `.info` with `tone-light`: violet, =. Violet, because cyan is the focus color.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| warning | `////////` | `.alert` with `tone-danger`. |
| info | `========` | `.alert.info` with `tone-light`. |
| no script | `////////` | The same. It is CSS. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by, or stops at the links and buttons in it. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `role="note"`: read in place, not announced. One that appears while the page is open needs `role="alert"`, and only that one.
- **name**: The title is a `<span>`. Make it a heading when the alert opens a section.
- **paint**: The rim and the shadow are CSS content with empty alt text. The title says it in words; the yellow only repeats it.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Say what happened in the title and what to do in the body. | Write "Error" in the title and nothing useful under it. |
| One alert on a page at a time. | Stack three. The third one is wallpaper. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.alert .info` | The hazard box, and its violet one. |
| class | `.lift .card .bar-title .body` | The card inside it, as in [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card). `tone-danger` for the warning, `tone-light` for info. |
| attr | `role="note"` | On the `.alert`. |

See also: [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast), [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card), [Badge](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/badge), [Empty](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/empty)

Limits:
- No close button. It stays until the page takes it away.
- Yellow or violet. Good news is a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast), not a lime alert.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div class="alert lift" role="note">
    <div class="card frame tone-danger">
      <span class="bar-title">Signal lost</span>
      <div class="body">
        <p>Probes from 3 regions are timing out. Check the load balancer in fra-1.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="alert info lift" role="note">
    <div class="card frame tone-light">
      <span class="bar-title">Heads up</span>
      <div class="body"><p>Maintenance window on Sunday at 03:00 UTC. Probes keep running.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

<a id="s-empty"></a>
### Empty

- Id: `s-empty`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/empty`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#empty`
- Caption: When there is nothing, say so and offer the next step.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui-toast`: shows a toast
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `card`: `.card .lift .bar-title .body`
  - `toast`: `.toast [data-aui-toast]`
- Use it for:
  - A list, a table or a search with nothing in it yet. Say so, and offer the one next step.
- Not for:
  - An error. Nothing loaded is not the same as nothing there: say what broke, in an [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert).
  - Loading. That is a [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton).

Anatomy:

```text
1 @@ NO WORK ORDERS @@@@@@@@
  :                       : ::
3 :   Nothing is broken.  : ::
  :   Enjoy it.           : ::
  :                       : ::
4 :     CREATE WORK ORDER : ::
2 - - - - - - - - - - - - - ::
    ::::::::::::::::::::::::::
```

1. **title** `.bar-title`: What is not there, in plain words: "No work orders". The top rim is @, as on every card.
2. **frame** `.card`: `tone-faint`: the quietest rim. Nothing to see, and it looks it.
3. **line** `.body p`: One line, muted. A joke is fine; blame is not.
4. **next step** `.btn-primary`: The one thing to do next, as a primary [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button).

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| empty | `- - - -` | The only state it has. When there is something, show the thing. |
| no script | `- - - -` | The card shows. The button does nothing, unless it is a link. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | To the button. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Presses it. |

Accessibility:
- **name**: The title is a `<span>`. Make it a heading when the card stands in for a whole section.
- **live**: It is not announced when it shows up. After a search that finds nothing, say so in a `role="status"` too.
- **paint**: The rims and the shadow are paint.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Offer one next step. | Offer four, or none. |
| Say why it is empty, when you know: "No results for fra-2". | Show a table with its headers and nothing under them. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.lift .card .tone-faint` | The card, faint. |
| class | `.bar-title .body` | The title on the rim, and the walls with the line and the button. |
| attr | `data-aui-toast` | On the button in the demo: a lime toast. Yours creates the thing. |

See also: [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card), [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert), [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- It does not know when a list is empty. Your script shows it and takes it away.

```html
<div class="lift">
  <div class="card frame tone-faint">
    <span class="bar-title">No work orders</span>
    <div class="body">
      <p class="muted">Nothing is broken. Enjoy it, it never lasts.</p>
      <div class="row">
        <button class="btn btn-primary frame tone-heavy" type="button" data-aui-toast="Work order created. So much for nothing."><span class="mid"><span class="label">Create work order</span></span></button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

<a id="s-progress"></a>
### Progress

- Id: `s-progress`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/progress`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#progress`
- Caption: How far along a task is, on the halftone bar. The spinner lives inside the button.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui="progress"`: draws the bar from aria-valuenow
  - `data-aui-fill`: runs the progress bar next to it
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `bar`: `.bar .slider .slider-track .progress`
- Use it for:
  - A task with a known end that takes more than a second: an export, an upload.
  - When you can say how far along it is. The number goes next to the bar.
- Not for:
  - A wait with no end you can measure. That is a [Spinner](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/spinner).
  - A value a person sets. That is a [Slider](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/slider).
  - Content loading into place. That is a [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton).

Anatomy:

```text
1 @@@@%#*+=:..............   42%
  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^
  2                         3
  =====================
4 :: / EXPORT REPORT ::
  =====================
```

1. **progress** `[role="progressbar"]`: `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and an `aria-label` that says what is running.
2. **bar** `.bar`: Paint, `aria-hidden`, drawn from `aria-valuenow`. 24 cells; `data-cells` sets how many.
3. **percent** `.pct`: The number, 4 characters, padded on the left so the bar does not move. `aria-hidden`: the value is on the progressbar.
4. **demo button** `[data-aui-fill]`: Runs the bar from 0 to 100 with a spinner in its label, for demos. Your task sets `aria-valuenow` instead.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| empty | `........` | 0: all dots. Where it starts. |
| running | `@@%#*+=.` | Full to `aria-valuenow`, 0 to 100, rounded. |
| done | `@@@@@@@@` | 100. The demo button says so in the status line next to it, or in a toast when there is none. |
| no script | `........` | The bar stays empty. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes the bar by. It is not a control. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | On the demo button: starts it. The button is `disabled` until it ends. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `role="progressbar"`: a screen reader reads its value as a percent when it gets there.
- **live**: It is not announced as it moves. Say the end in the `role="status"` next to it: `data-aui-done` does that for the demo button.
- **state**: The demo button is `disabled` while it runs, so it cannot start twice.
- **paint**: The bar and the number are `aria-hidden`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Say what is running, in the `aria-label` and on the button. | Label it "Progress". |
| Say when it is done, in words. | Let the bar reach 100 and leave people to notice. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui="progress"` | On the `role="progressbar"`. Draws the bar and the number from `aria-valuenow`. |
| attr | `aria-valuenow` | 0 to 100. Change it and the bar redraws. |
| attr | `data-cells="24"` | How many cells the bar has. 24 when missing. Followed live. |
| attr | `data-aui-fill` | On a button: runs the nearest bar from 0 to 100, for demos. |
| attr | `data-aui-done` | With `data-aui-fill`: what it says at the end. "Done." when missing. |
| class | `.progress .bar .pct` | The box, the bar and the number. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.progress(el, pct)` | Sets `aria-valuenow`, rounded, 0 to 100. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.get(el)` | `draw()`, `set(p)`, and `value`. |

See also: [Spinner](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/spinner), [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton), [Slider](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/slider), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- Whole percents, 0 to 100. `aria-valuemax` is not read: 100 is the end.
- No look for a task that failed. Say it in the status line, or in a [Toast](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/toast).

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div>
    <div class="progress" role="progressbar" aria-label="Export progress" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="0" data-aui="progress">
      <span class="bar" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="pct" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <button class="btn frame tone-light" type="button" data-aui-fill data-aui-done="Exported report."><span class="mid"><span class="label">Export report</span></span></button>
    <span class="muted" role="status"></span>
  </div>
</div>
```

<a id="s-skeleton"></a>
### Skeleton

- Id: `s-skeleton`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/skeleton`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#skeleton`
- Caption: Loading is a wave moving through the ramp.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui="skeleton"`: draws the silhouette and the wave
- CSS blocks:
  - `skeleton`: `.skel`
- Use it for:
  - A card or a list that is loading, when you know its shape: a silhouette where it will be.
  - Waits of a second or two.
- Not for:
  - A wait with a known end. That is [Progress](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/progress).
  - Nothing to show. That is [Empty](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/empty).
  - A wait of more than a few seconds. Say what is happening, with a [Spinner](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/spinner) and words.

Anatomy:

```text
1 - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
2 .:=+*#*+=:.
  .:=+*##*+=:..:=+*##*+=:..:=
  =+*##*+=:..:=+*##*+

  - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
3 "Loading", read, not drawn
```

1. **box** `.skel`: A `<pre>`, `aria-hidden`. The kit fills it with a card: a rule, three lines, a gap, a rule. 12 to 60 characters, as wide as its box.
2. **wave** `.skel`: The lines are the ramp, `.:=+*#`, with a wave moving through them 8 times a second.
3. **label** `.vh`: "Loading", for screen readers only, next to it.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| loading | `.:=+*#*+` | The wave moves through the ramp, only while it is on screen. |
| reduced motion | `.:=+*#*+` | One frame, still. |
| no script | ` ` | Empty. The `<pre>` has nothing in it. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. Nothing in it takes the focus. |

Accessibility:
- **paint**: `aria-hidden` on the `<pre>`: nobody hears rows of dots.
- **name**: "Loading" is a `.vh` span, read in place. It is not announced.
- **live**: When the content arrives, it takes the skeleton's place. Announce it only if people wait for it.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Match the shape of what is coming. | Show a card silhouette where a table will be. |
| Swap it for the content in one go. | Leave it up after the content has landed next to it. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui="skeleton"` | On a `<pre class="skel">`. Draws the card and runs the wave. |
| class | `.skel` | The box. Muted, 6 rows tall at least. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.get(el).draw()` | Draws the next frame. The kit calls it by itself; you rarely need to. |

See also: [Spinner](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/spinner), [Progress](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/progress), [Empty](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/empty)

Limits:
- One shape: a card. For a list or a table, draw your own lines of the ramp.
- It does not say how long. A long wait needs words.

```html
<div>
  <span class="vh">Loading</span>
  <pre class="skel" aria-hidden="true" data-aui="skeleton"></pre>
</div>
```

<a id="s-spinner"></a>
### Spinner

- Id: `s-spinner`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/spinner`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#spinner`
- Caption: Five ways to wait.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui="spinner"`: animates data-kind, still under reduced motion
- CSS blocks:
  - `spinner`: `.spins [data-aui="spinner"]`
- Use it for:
  - A wait with no end you can measure, inside the thing that waits: a button, a row, a status line.
  - Short waits. Past a few seconds, add words.
- Not for:
  - A task with a known end. That is [Progress](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/progress).
  - A page loading its content. That is a [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton).

Anatomy:

```text
1 /        classic
  =+*      ramp
  [  =  ]  bounce
  ..       dots
  @%#*+=:. fill
  ^^^^^^^^ ^^^^
  2        3
```

1. **grid** `.spins`: The demo's grid, 14 characters a column. Your spinner sits where the wait is.
2. **spinner** `[data-aui="spinner"]`: A `<b>` or a `<span>`, 8 characters wide at least, magenta. The kit writes a new frame into it 9 times a second.
3. **words** `span`: What is waiting, in words. The spinner alone says nothing.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| spinning | `/` | A new frame every 110ms, only while it is on screen. |
| reduced motion | `|` | The first frame, still. \| for classic. |
| no script | ` ` | Empty. Nothing moves. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Passes it by. A spinner is not a control. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: The demo is `role="img"` with an `aria-label`. A spinner of yours sits next to words that say what is waiting.
- **paint**: The frames are text: a screen reader that lands on one reads "slash". Give a spinner `aria-hidden="true"` and say the wait in words.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Put it where the wait is, next to the words for it. | Spin in a corner while the button a person pressed looks idle. |
| Take it away the moment the wait ends. | Leave it spinning after an error. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui="spinner"` | On a `<b>` or a `<span>`. Runs the frames. |
| attr | `data-kind="classic"` | `classic`, `ramp`, `bounce`, `dots` or `fill`. Classic when missing. Followed live. |
| class | `.spins` | A grid of them, for a page like this one. |

See also: [Progress](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/progress), [Skeleton](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/skeleton), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- No stop call. Take the element away, or its `data-aui`, and the kit tears it down.

```html
<div class="spins" role="img" aria-label="Loading indicators">
  <span><b data-aui="spinner" data-kind="classic"></b>classic</span>
  <span><b data-aui="spinner" data-kind="ramp"></b>ramp</span>
  <span><b data-aui="spinner" data-kind="bounce"></b>bounce</span>
  <span><b data-aui="spinner" data-kind="dots"></b>dots</span>
  <span><b data-aui="spinner" data-kind="fill"></b>fill</span>
</div>
```

<a id="s-toast"></a>
### Toast

- Id: `s-toast`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/toast`
- Group: Feedback
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#toast`
- Caption: One line, typed in from the left. Lime for good news, yellow for the other kind.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui-toast`: shows a toast
  - `data-aui-toast-err`: shows a yellow toast
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `toast`: `.toast [data-aui-toast]`
- Use it for:
  - Saying that something happened because of what a person did: saved, copied, sent.
  - Yellow, `data-aui-toast-err`, for what did not work, when the person can try again.
- Not for:
  - Anything a person must read or act on. It is gone in 3.6 seconds. That is an [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert).
  - A question. That is the dialog in [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card).
  - Errors on a form. They go under the field, in an [Input](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/input).

Anatomy:

```text
1  @@ Changes saved.
2  !! Something broke.
  ==================
3 :: SAVE CHANGES ::
  ==================
```

1. **good** `.toast`: Lime, marked @@. One line, typed in from the left.
2. **bad** `.toast.err`: `.err`: yellow, marked !!.
3. **button** `[data-aui-toast]`: Any button with `data-aui-toast="Saved."`: the words are the value.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| hidden | ` ` | Clipped to nothing, until the next one. |
| on | ` @@ Save` | Types in, in 12 steps, and stays 3.6 seconds. On a desktop it sits at the bottom; on a phone, at the top. |
| error | ` !! Nope` | `.err`: yellow. |
| in a dialog | ` @@ Save` | While a modal dialog is open it goes inside it, so it sits on top and is read out. |
| no script | ` ` | Nothing shows. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space` | On the button: shows it. |
| `Tab` | Never lands on the toast. Nothing in it takes the focus. |

Accessibility:
- **live**: `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`: read after whatever is being said, and the focus stays put.
- **state**: The kit makes the region first and writes the words a beat later, so the change is heard.
- **name**: @@ and !! are part of the text, so a screen reader reads them before the words.
- **touch**: On a phone it drops in from the top, away from the thumb that tapped.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Say what happened, in a few words: "Changes saved." | Say "Success!". |
| Show one for what a person did. | Toast every background sync. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui-toast` | On a button: a lime toast on click. The words are the value: `data-aui-toast="Saved."`. |
| attr | `data-aui-toast-err` | On a button: a yellow one. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.toast(msg, err)` | Shows one from a script. `err` makes it yellow. |
| class | `.toast .err .on` | Made by the kit, once, at the end of the page. |

See also: [Alert](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/alert), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button), [Card and dialog](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/card)

Limits:
- One at a time. A new one replaces the last.
- No close button, no action in it, no pause on hover.

```html
<div class="row">
  <button class="btn frame tone-light" type="button" data-aui-toast="Changes saved."><span class="mid"><span class="label">Save changes</span></span></button>
  <button class="btn btn-danger frame tone-danger" type="button" data-aui-toast-err="Something broke. It was you."><span class="mid"><span class="label">Break something</span></span></button>
</div>
```

## Navigation

<a id="s-breadcrumb"></a>
### Breadcrumb

- Id: `s-breadcrumb`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/breadcrumb`
- Group: Navigation
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#breadcrumb`
- Caption: Slashes do the separating. The current page is a slab.
- Behaviors: none, HTML and CSS only
- CSS blocks:
  - `crumbs`: `.crumbs`
- Use it for:
  - Where this page sits in a tree of pages, and the way back up: Workspace / Projects / Signal.
  - Sites more than two levels deep.
- Not for:
  - The steps of a task. Number them in a plain list.
  - Views of one thing. That is [Tabs](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tabs).
  - A site one level deep. The page title says it all.

Anatomy:

```text
Workspace / Projects /  Signal
^^^^^^^^^ ^            ^^^^^^^^
1         2            3
```

1. **link** `a`: A link to the page above, muted. It underlines on hover.
2. **slash** `li + li`: / in magenta, CSS content with empty alt text.
3. **current** `[aria-current]`: This page: `aria-current="page"` on its `<li>`, the words in a `<span>` on an ink slab. Not a link.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| link | `Projects` | Muted. |
| hover | `Projects` | Ink and underlined. Mouse only. |
| focus | `Projects` | A slab in the focus color. |
| current | ` Signal` | An ink slab, bold. |
| no script | `Projects` | Works as it is. They are links. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | To each link. |
| `Enter` | Follows it. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` around an `<ol>`: a landmark, and a list in order.
- **state**: `aria-current="page"` on the last one: read as "current page".
- **paint**: The slashes are CSS content with empty alt text.
- **touch**: Each link takes the tap 12px above and below: 45px tall.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Start at the top of the tree and end at this page. | Put in the pages a person happened to click through. That is the Back button. |
| Use the page titles, word for word. | Shorten "Projects" to "Proj." |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| class | `.crumbs` | On the `<ol>`. |
| attr | `aria-current="page"` | On the `<li>` of this page. Its words go in a `<span>`. |
| attr | `aria-label="Breadcrumb"` | On the `<nav>`. |

See also: [Tabs](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tabs), [Pagination](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/pagination)

Limits:
- No collapsing. A long trail wraps onto a second row.
- No menu on a crumb.

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="crumbs">
    <li><a href="#">Workspace</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Projects</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page"><span>Signal</span></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

<a id="s-pagination"></a>
### Pagination

- Id: `s-pagination`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/pagination`
- Group: Navigation
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#pagination`
- Caption: Brackets around every page, a slab under the current one.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui="pagination"`: draws the pages from data-pages and data-page
- CSS blocks:
  - `ibtn`: `.ibtn`
  - `pagination`: `[data-aui="pagination"]`
- Use it for:
  - Long lists split into pages a person moves through: results, orders, logs.
  - When the page number matters. With `data-href`, page 3 is a link that stays page 3.
- Not for:
  - A few items. Show them all.
  - The steps of a task. That is Back and Next, two [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)s.
  - A feed people scroll. A button at the end that loads more.

Anatomy:

```text
1 [<] [1] .. [3] .. [9] [>]
  ^^^     ^^ ^^^
  2       3  4
5 Page 3 of 9.
```

1. **nav** `[data-aui="pagination"]`: A `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`, empty. The kit draws into it from `data-pages` and `data-page`. This is the phone width; a wider box shows a page on each side of the current one.
2. **step** `.ibtn`: [&lt;] and [&gt;]. `disabled` on the first and the last page.
3. **gap** `.muted`: .. where pages are left out. `aria-hidden`.
4. **current** `[aria-current="page"]`: The page you are on: an ink slab, brackets and all.
5. **status** `[role="status"]`: The nearest one says "Page 3 of 9."

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| page | `[4]` | A number in brackets. |
| current | `[3]` | An ink slab, and `aria-current="page"`. |
| focus | `[4]` | A slab in the focus color, brackets and all. On the current page too. |
| disabled | `[<]` | [&lt;] on the first page, [&gt;] on the last: gray and `disabled`. |
| narrow | `[3] ..` | Under 374px it drops the neighbours instead of shrinking the targets. |
| no script | ` ` | Nothing is drawn. Put plain links in the nav as a fallback: the script replaces them. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | To each page, and to [&lt;] and [&gt;]. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Goes to that page. The focus moves to the new current page. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: A `<nav>` with an `aria-label`: a landmark.
- **name**: Each button is named: "Page 3", "Previous page", "Next page".
- **state**: `aria-current="page"` on the page you are on.
- **live**: The status line is `role="status"`: it reads "Page 3 of 9." after a pick.
- **touch**: Every page is 5 characters wide and 45px tall.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use `data-href` when each page has an address. | Use buttons for pages people want to share or bookmark. |
| Say the total: "Page 3 of 9." | Hide how many pages there are. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui="pagination"` | On an empty `<nav>`. Draws the pages. |
| attr | `data-pages="9"` | How many pages. 9 when missing. Followed live. |
| attr | `data-page` | The page, from 1. Past the end, the last one is drawn and the number is kept. |
| attr | `data-href="?page={n}"` | Draws links instead of buttons. A link goes, so no event. |
| class | `.ibtn` | Each page, and [&lt;] [&gt;]: a character in brackets. |
| event | `aui:change` | On the `<nav>`, when a person picks a page. `detail`: `{ page }`. Buttons only. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.pagination(el)` | `set(n)`, and `page` and `pages`. |

See also: [Breadcrumb](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/breadcrumb), [Tabs](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/tabs), [Button](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/button)

Limits:
- No page size picker and no field to type a page.
- With `data-href` each pick loads a new page: no event, and the status changes when it lands.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <nav class="row" aria-label="Pagination" data-aui="pagination" data-pages="9" data-page="3"></nav>
  <p class="muted status" role="status">Page 3 of 9.</p>
</div>
```

<a id="s-tabs"></a>
### Tabs

- Id: `s-tabs`, address `https://ascii.fedekotek.design#components/tabs`
- Group: Navigation
- In the kit: yes, `kit/starter.html#tabs`
- Caption: The active tab is a solid slab. Arrow keys move between tabs.
- Behaviors:
  - `data-aui="tabs"`: arrows, Home and End move between tabs
- CSS blocks:
  - `button`: `.btn`
  - `tabs`: `.tablist .tab .tabpanel`
- Use it for:
  - Two to six views of one thing, one at a time: a preview and its code, settings by topic.
  - Panels that are already on the page. The arrows open each one on the way past.
- Not for:
  - Moving between pages. Tabs swap panels, links go places. For the trail back, [Breadcrumb](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/breadcrumb).
  - A value for a form. That is a [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup): it is sent with the form.
  - More tabs than fit on one line. The strip wraps and stops reading as one row.

Anatomy:

```text
    2         3
    v         v
    BUTTON    HTML    CSS
1 =========================
4 Only the picked panel shows.
```

1. **strip** `.tablist`: `role="tablist"`, where `data-aui="tabs"` goes. Its rule is violet.
2. **picked** `.tab[aria-selected="true"]`: An ink slab with a violet and magenta edge. The only tab in the Tab order.
3. **tab** `.tab`: A real `<button>`, a muted word until it is picked.
4. **panel** `.tabpanel`: `role="tabpanel"`, one per tab, after the strip and in the same order. The others are `hidden`.

| State | Looks like | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| rest | `  HTML` | A muted word. |
| hover | `  HTML` | Ink. Mouse only. |
| focus | `  HTML` | A slab in the focus color. |
| picked | ` BUTTON` | An ink slab with the edge. |
| no script | `  HTML` | The panels show or hide as the HTML has them. The tabs do nothing. |

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Lands on the picked tab. Tab again goes to its panel. |
| `Left`, `Right` | The previous or the next tab, and its panel. It wraps around. |
| `Home`, `End` | The first or the last tab. |

Accessibility:
- **role**: `tablist`, `tab` and `tabpanel`, in the markup. The kit links each tab to its panel with `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby`, and makes the ids.
- **name**: Give the tablist an `aria-label` that says what the views are of.
- **state**: `aria-selected` on the picked tab. Only that one has `tabindex="0"`, so the strip is one Tab stop.
- **focus**: A panel with `tabindex="0"` is a Tab stop of its own, marked by a bar in the focus color on its left.
- **paint**: The rule under the strip is paint.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Name tabs with a noun or two: HTML, CSS. | Put a sentence on a tab. The strip wraps and stops being a row. |
| Start on the tab most people need. | Start on Settings because it was built last. |

| Kind | Name | Does |
|---|---|---|
| attr | `data-aui="tabs"` | On the `role="tablist"`. Click, the arrows, Home and End pick a tab. |
| attr | `aria-selected="true"` | On the tab that starts picked. The first one, when none says so. |
| attr | `aria-controls` | Optional. Names a panel by id, for panels that do not sit next to the strip. |
| class | `.tablist .tab .tabpanel` | The strip, each tab, each panel. |
| event | `aui:change` | On the tablist, when a person picks another tab. `detail`: `{ tab, index }`. Not on load, not for `select()`. |
| call | `ASCIIUI.tabs(el)` | `select(i)` takes an index or a tab. `index` and `tab` say which one is picked. |

See also: [Toggle group](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/togglegroup), [Breadcrumb](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/breadcrumb), [Pagination](https://ascii.fedekotek.design/#components/pagination)

Limits:
- The panels sit next to the strip, in one element around both, unless `aria-controls` names them. Two tab sets need two wrappers.
- Up and Down do nothing. The strip is a row.
- A panel shows as soon as the arrow reaches its tab. For a panel that has to load, that is a request per key press.

```html
<div>
  <div class="tablist" role="tablist" aria-label="Views" data-aui="tabs">
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="true" type="button">Button</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1" type="button">HTML</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1" type="button">CSS</button>
  </div>
  <div class="tabpanel" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0">
    <div class="row">
      <button class="btn btn-primary frame tone-heavy" type="button"><span class="mid"><span class="label">Publish site</span></span></button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="tabpanel" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0" hidden>
    <pre>&lt;button class="btn btn-primary
  frame tone-heavy"&gt;
  &lt;span class="mid"&gt;
    &lt;span class="label"&gt;
      Publish site
    &lt;/span&gt;
  &lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/button&gt;</pre>
  </div>
  <div class="tabpanel" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0" hidden>
    <pre>.tone-heavy {
  --h: "@@@@@@@@@@@@...";
  --s: "@@";
}
.frame::before,
.frame::after {
  content: var(--h);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.mid::before,
.mid::after {
  content: var(--s);
}</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```
